title: Settings overview and navigation
summary: How the Settings area is organised, who can see which sections, and how to find any setting fast.

body.text: **Settings** is the single place to configure your workspace, customer channels, operational policies and security. Open it from the main navigation. What you see depends on your access level.
Who sees what

If you are an **owner (admin)**, you see every settings section. Everyone else sees only **My Account** — your own profile, password, two-factor authentication, passkeys and device notifications. All other sections are admin-only.
How settings are grouped

items: **You** — My Account and Notifications.
**CRM** — Pipeline, Quotes, Import.
**Workshop** — Bookings and slots.
**Catalog** — Products, Stock labels, Library.
**Comms & Marketing** — Email, Automations.
**Organisation** — Company profile, Team & access, Portal access, Documents, Signing workflows, Security, Backup & recovery, Sessions & devices, Integrations, System Log.

body.text: Finding a setting

The settings sidebar is searchable, and the same catalogue powers the application-wide search. Search by name or by keyword (for example "logo", "webhook", "2FA", "stock") to jump straight to the right panel.

Some sections open as their own full page (Company profile, Team & access, Pipelines, Security, Backup & recovery, Sessions, Portal access, Documents, Signing workflows). Others open as a tab within the main Settings page.

title: My Account: profile, password and email signature
summary: Manage your own password, mobile number and email signature from the My Account tab.

body.text: **My Account** is the one settings tab every user can open. It shows your name, email and whether you are an Owner or a Member, and lets you manage your own sign-in and signature.
Change your password

items: Open Settings and go to My Account.
Expand **Password** and choose Change.
Enter your current password, then a new password of at least 12 characters containing letters and numbers.
Save. The new password must be different from your current one.

body.text: Changing your password signs out all your other devices immediately. Your current session stays active.
Email signature

Expand **Email signature** to preview your branded signature. Add **My mobile number** so it appears in the signature. Leave **Custom signature HTML** blank to keep the branded signature (recommended); fill it in only if you need a fully custom block.
Push notifications
The **Push notifications** panel opts this specific device in to alerts when a lead, DM or signed quote comes in. Each phone or computer opts in separately — see the Notifications article for detail.

title: Two-factor authentication and passkeys
summary: Add a second sign-in step with an authenticator app, backup codes, email codes or a passkey.

body.text: Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds a second step at sign-in, protecting your account even if your password leaks. Set it up from **My Account**. Your status shows as On or Off.
Set up an authenticator app

items: In My Account, expand **Two-factor authentication** and choose Set up.
Select **Set up authenticator app**.
Scan the QR code with Google Authenticator, Authy or 1Password (or enter the shown key manually).
Enter the 6-digit code the app displays and choose Verify & enable.
Save the one-time **backup codes** shown — each works once if you lose your phone. They are not shown again.

body.text: Store your backup codes somewhere safe and separate from your phone. Without them, losing your authenticator device can lock you out.
Turn 2FA off
Expand Two-factor authentication, enter a current authenticator code, and choose **Disable 2FA**.
Email sign-in codes (backup)
Tick **Also allow email sign-in codes as a backup** to receive a code by email at sign-in. It is a useful fallback, but be aware your email inbox then becomes part of your account security.
Passkeys

Expand **Passkeys** to add a passkey (fingerprint, face or device PIN) for password-free sign-in. Each passkey can be given a nickname; the panel shows when each was created and last used, and lets you remove ones you no longer use.

title: Notifications and push alerts
summary: Opt each device in to push, and (admins) choose which events notify the whole team.

body.text: Notifications are controlled in two places: **per device** (each user, on each device) and **team-wide** (admins decide which event types are allowed to notify anyone).
Turn on push for this device

items: Open Settings and go to Notifications (or the Push panel in My Account).
Expand **Push on this device** and choose Manage.
Allow notifications when your browser or phone prompts.

body.text: Each phone and computer opts in separately. Install the app on your phone (add to home screen) for lock-screen notifications.
Choose what sends a notification (admins)
The **What sends a notification** list applies to the whole team's devices — unticking a type silences it everywhere. Available types include:

items: New lead, Social DMs, WhatsApp messages, Bot hand-offs
Service bookings, Portal service requests, Support cases, Warranty claims, Profile change requests
Quote opened, Quote / job card signed, Quote declined or changes
Google reviews, Email replies, Referral fees, Competitor changes
System errors (throttled to 1 per 30 min), Security & AI health, Backup failures (throttled to 1 per day), Meeting reminders

body.text: Editing the team-wide list is owner-only. Members can still manage push on their own devices.

title: Company profile and branding
summary: Set the business details that fill merge fields and the branded footer on your documents.

body.text: **Company profile** is the single source of truth for your business details. It fills the {{company.*}} merge fields and the branded footer in documents that use them (the Document Builder, e-signature documents and Document Studio). Only owners can open it.
Fields you can set

rows: Contact details in the footer and merge fields

items: Open Settings, then Company profile.
Fill in the fields you want to use.
Choose Save company profile.

body.text: Blank fields fall back to the built-in defaults. The classic quote, invoice and agreement print templates are being migrated to read from here.

title: Managing team members and user security
summary: Add users, disable or reactivate accounts, revoke sessions, reset 2FA and set the idle sign-out policy.

body.text: User accounts are managed in two places: the **Team** tab in Settings (quick add and per-user controls) and the **Team & access** page (full user-security table, teams and roles).
Add a team member

items: In Settings, open the Team tab.
Expand **Add a team member**.
Enter their full name, email and a password of at least 12 characters containing letters and numbers.
Choose Add team member.

body.text: New users are created as Members and automatically assigned the Sales rep role. Adjust their roles afterwards on the Team & access page. Emails must be unique.
Per-user controls

In the Team table, each other user has controls to **Make admin / Make member**, toggle legacy access modules (CRM, Workshop, Reports, Social Inbox — fallbacks for screens not yet on role-based permissions), and **Reset 2FA**. Resetting 2FA signs the user out and lets them sign in with only their password until they reconfigure it.
User security (Team & access page)
The **User security** table lists every user with status, last login and failed-login count. For any user other than yourself you can:

items: **Revoke sessions** — sign the user out of every device.
**Disable** — block sign-in entirely; **Reactivate** to restore access.

body.text: Disabling a user or revoking their sessions takes effect on their next request, not necessarily instantly.
Auto sign-out policy
On the Team tab, set **Auto sign-out after inactivity** (15 minutes up to 24 hours). Everyone still re-signs in at least once per absolute session window regardless of this setting.

title: Roles and permissions
summary: Bundle granular permissions into roles, then assign roles to people for fine-grained access control.

body.text: Access is controlled by **roles** — named bundles of permissions that you assign to users. Manage them under **Team & access → Roles & permissions**. Owners always have every permission; everything else is granted through roles.
Create a role

items: On the Team & access page, choose **Create role**.
Give it a name (e.g. "Sales manager") and an optional description.
Create it, then expand the role to tick the permissions it should include.
Choose **Save permissions**.

body.text: Permissions are grouped by category (leads, contacts, quotes, documents, cases, vehicles, job cards, reports, teams, roles, audit and more). Most modules offer view-all versus view-owned scopes plus create, edit, manage and delete actions — for example **leads.view_all** versus **leads.view_owned**, or **quotes.change_status**.
Roles marked System are built in. You can view and adjust their permissions but they are intended as sensible defaults.
Assign roles to people

items: Scroll to **Role assignments**.
For each user, tick the roles they should have.
Choose Save on that user's row.

body.text: "Owned" scopes let someone see only records they created, are assigned to, or that belong to their team. Use view-owned roles for reps and view-all roles for managers.

title: Teams and lead visibility
summary: Group members into teams to drive team-level lead ownership and view-owned visibility.

body.text: **Teams** group members so that view-owned permissions extend across a team, not just to individuals. A user with view-owned access sees records they own plus records belonging to any team they are a member of or manage. Manage teams under **Team & access → Teams**.
Create a team

items: On the Team & access page, choose **Create team**.
Enter a name (e.g. "Sales floor"), optionally pick a manager, and add a description.
Create it.

body.text: Manage members
Expand a team to add or remove members, change its manager, edit its description, or toggle it Active. The team manager and every member can see the team's leads under owned scopes.
Viewing teams needs the teams.view permission; creating and editing them needs teams.manage. Without manage rights you see teams read-only.

title: Sales pipelines and stages
summary: Configure separate sales processes and their stages, colours, probabilities and closed results.

body.text: **Sales pipelines** let you run separate retail, fleet, hospitality, partner and service-sales processes, each with its own stages. Manage them under Settings → Pipeline (Team & access users need the pipelines.manage permission).
Create a pipeline

items: On the Pipelines page, choose **Create pipeline**.
Name it, pick a type (Retail, Fleet/B2B, Hospitality, Partner/Dealer, Service upsell or Other sales), and add an optional description.
Optionally tick **Make this the default pipeline**.
Create it.

body.text: Configure stages

Expand a pipeline to manage its stages. For each stage you can set the name, colour, default win **probability**, a **stale after days** threshold, and whether it is a **Closed stage** with a closed result of Won or Lost. Use the up/down arrows to reorder stages.
Archiving a pipeline is only possible when it has no active or historical leads, and the default pipeline cannot be archived.
There is also a simpler legacy Pipeline stages editor (name, colour and order) on the main Settings page. A stage still holding leads cannot be deleted.

title: Customer portal access
summary: Grant delegated account or fleet access to portal users and review customer profile-change requests.

body.text: **Portal access** administers who can see what in the customer portal, and approves changes customers request to their own details. It needs the portal_access.manage permission.
Grant delegated access
Delegation lets one portal user (a contact with an email) see another account's or a fleet's records — for example a company admin viewing all vehicles on a fleet.

items: Open Settings → Portal access.
In **Grant contact/account access** or **Grant fleet access**, choose the portal user, then the contact/account or fleet to expose.
Pick a role — Viewer, Manager or Owner — and choose Grant access.

body.text: Active grants are listed with their role and status. Choose **Revoke** to end a grant.
Review profile-change requests

When a customer requests changes to their contact details, they appear under **Pending profile changes**. Review the proposed values, then **Approve & apply** (with an optional note) or **Reject** (a reason is required).

title: Security runbook
summary: Run automated checks on keys, exposure, backups and accounts, and track your security score over time.

body.text: The **Security runbook** runs automated self-checks on keys, surface exposure, backups and accounts, and grades your posture as a score out of 100. It is owner-only and lives under Settings → Security.
Running the checks

items: Open Settings → Security.
Use the run button to check on demand; the sweep runs live self-probes and can take up to a minute.
Review each result — Pass, Warn or Fail — with the suggested fix for anything that isn't passing.

body.text: The top strip shows your **Score** (passed / warn / failed), the **Last run** date, **AI health** (OK, Off or Down) and **AI usage** for the month (calls and token counts).
The runbook auto-runs on the 1st of every month. A History panel keeps an accountability trail of past scores.

title: Backup and recovery
summary: Monitor automated backups, verify retained packages, and follow the guided recovery runbook.

body.text: **Backup & recovery** monitors your automated database backups and asset snapshots, and documents the safe path to restore. It is owner-only, under Settings → Backup & recovery.
What runs automatically

A scheduled job creates an encrypted, portable backup package daily at 02:00 UTC (04:00 SAST) and verifies it after upload. The newest 30 database packages are retained; asset snapshots are content-addressed and deduplicated. The dashboard shows protection status, copy counts, total size and the last verification.
Run or verify on demand

items: Choose **Run backup** to create a fresh restore point now.
Use **Verify** on any retained package to confirm it is intact.
Download the **Encrypted file** for off-site safekeeping if needed.

body.text: Recovery runbook

Recovery is deliberately guided, not one-click: (1) restore the database in Neon via point-in-time or a recovery branch; (2) validate a staging deployment against that branch; (3) pause writes, cut over the production connection and run smoke checks, keeping the old branch until sign-off.

Keep the SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY stored separately from the app. Downloaded portable files cannot be opened without the exact key used to create them. Portable restore is an emergency path — follow docs/backup-and-recovery.md during an incident.

title: Sessions and devices
summary: Review every active sign-in across the team and revoke a device or a whole user immediately.

body.text: **Sessions & devices** lists every active sign-in across the team, grouped by user, so you can spot and cut off access fast. It is owner-only, under Settings → Sessions & devices.
What each session shows
Each entry shows the device (browser and OS), IP address, when it signed in and when it was last active. Mobile app (installed PWA) sessions are flagged and use a 7-day session window.
Revoke access

items: Open Settings → Sessions & devices.
To sign out one device, choose **Revoke** on that session.
To sign a user out everywhere, choose **Sign out all** on their card.

body.text: Use Sign out all when a laptop or phone is lost, or when off-boarding someone. Pair it with Disable on the Team & access page to block re-sign-in.

title: Integrations: WhatsApp, Meta, Google, SMS, AI and lead intake
summary: Connect messaging channels, reviews, SMS codes, AI Assist and the website lead-intake API.

body.text: The **Integrations** tab (owner-only) connects your external channels and services. Each row shows a Connected or Not set up status. Secrets are stored encrypted and shown as password fields.
Facebook & Instagram (Meta)

Powers lead ads and Messenger/Instagram DMs. Add the webhook callback URL (shown in the panel) with the leadgen and messages fields, using the generated **Verify token** (regenerable). Save the **Page access token** (System User) and the **App secret** that verifies webhook signatures.
WhatsApp Business (Cloud API)

Add the WhatsApp product in your Meta app, register your number, and subscribe the WhatsApp webhook to the messages field (same verify token and app secret as Meta). Save the **Phone number ID** and a permanent System User **access token**.
Other connectors

rows: New reviews appear in the Social inbox with a push
OTPs for website vehicle verification (falls back to email)
Message check, lead research, optional auto-research
POST leads from your website/landing pages

body.text: AI Assist only makes suggestions — it never changes data. Optionally tick auto-research to research every new lead within about 15 minutes. Regenerating an intake or verify token invalidates the old one immediately.

title: Documents, templates and the document repository
summary: Manage print templates, Document Studio, reusable clauses, the Document Builder and the shared file repository.

body.text: The **Documents** hub (owner-only) manages every document surface: print templates, free-form Studio documents and the shared file repository. It opens with three tabs plus the Document Builder.
Templates

Templates cover the eight built-in document types (quote, invoice, agreement, indemnity, delivery note, job card, service report, warranty claim). For each type you can create a new template from defaults or by copying an existing one, mark one as **Default** for new documents, duplicate, edit or delete (the default can't be deleted).
Studio

Document Studio builds free-form documents. Create **Studio templates**, write **Reusable clauses** (payment terms, warranty text, indemnities) to insert anywhere, and generate a **New document** by picking a template and linking a customer, quote or deal — merge fields fill in and are frozen into the document. Documents can be marked draft or final and exported to PDF.
Document Builder
The **Document Builder** offers drag-and-drop blocks for flowing, multi-page, sealed PDFs. Open it from the banner at the top of the Documents page.
Repository

The **Repository** holds every signed quote, invoice, proof of payment, delivery note, photo and upload. Filter by file name, tag, what it is filed on (customer, vehicle, quote or unfiled) and whether to include version history, and upload new files directly.

title: Signing workflows
summary: Design approval chains that decide who signs, in what order, and the rules that route them.

body.text: **Signing workflows** (owner-only) design who signs a document, in what order, and the rules that route approvals — for example requiring manager approval above a value threshold.

items: Open Settings → Signing workflows.
Enter a name (e.g. "Manager approval over R500k") and choose **Create**.
Open the new workflow to design its signer steps and routing rules in the visual builder.
Saved workflows list their number of signer steps and when they were last updated.

body.text: Workflows use a node-based builder similar to the chatbot flow editor. Archived workflows are hidden from the list.

title: Catalog settings: products and stock labels
summary: Maintain the product catalogue and the organisational stock labels used to flag units.

body.text: Catalog settings cover your **Products** catalogue and **Stock labels**, both reached from the Catalog group in Settings. Products is admin-gated.
Stock labels
Stock labels are organisational tags kept **separate** from a unit's lifecycle status (incoming → delivered). Use them to flag demo units, showroom stock, consignment, management holds and the like.

items: Open Settings → Stock labels.
Under **Add a label**, enter a name (e.g. Demo unit, Consignment, Management hold) and pick a colour.
Choose Add label.
To delete a label, choose **Remove** — this clears it from any units carrying it.

body.text: Products
The **Products** section manages your catalogue and pricing used across quotes and stock. It opens the products management screen embedded in Settings.
The Library section (also under Catalog) manages the shared document library of files and attachments.
